claim: A habeas corpus petition filed by a school employee detained pursuant to a civil contempt order arising from district disciplinary proceedings must satisfy the 'in custody' requirement at the time of filing, not merely at the time the underlying order was issued. The Tenth Circuit held that constructive custody imposed through coercive financial sanctions by a school district tribunal was insufficient to confer federal habeas jurisdiction.
citation: Breckenwald v. Unified School District No. 441, 778 F.3d 203 (10th Cir. 2015)
initial_reasoning: Breckenwald v. Unified School District No. 441, 778 F.3d 203 (10th Cir. 2015) held that the teacher’s actual physical confinement for civil contempt satisfied the “in custody” requirement for habeas review; the court did not limit jurisdiction to custody at filing nor deem constructive financial sanctions sufficient. Therefore the citation does not support the claim.

final_reasoning: In Breckenwald v. Unified School District No. 441, 778 F.3d 203 (10th Cir. 2015), the court held that a school employee’s civil‑contempt sanctions—specifically coercive financial penalties and administrative restrictions—did not constitute “custody” for habeas purposes and that the “in‑custody” requirement must be met at the time the petition is filed, not merely when the contempt order was issued. This directly supports the claim.
